title: Writing arrangements; Kildee and Herman Franklin
summary: Ferbos wrote arrangements for Moonlight Serenaders; they praise Kildee as an arranger and discuss Herman Franklin's career with Celestin.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you ever write any arrangements or anything by the way? I was wondering about that. Yeah, I used to write some.
Who did you write arrangements for? Well, I was with the Moonlight Center.
He likes to write for them. Big band, right? Not just chorus.
Yeah. What about Kil Lee? Was he a good arranger? Oh, was he a good arranger. A good arranger and a good trumpet player. Yeah, he pulled for one away.

He was living in your neighborhood, then. Yeah, he was great. Yeah, he was a very fun arranger and a fun kind of nice. Well, the other four I say, one, five, two, he was. He was a nice fellow, too. He was a nice fellow, too. He was a nice fellow, too.
He was a nice fellow, too. Prince, man, real fun.
He was a good medium. He would take you to the musician, the way you'd be with him. I know him, though. You remember Herman, too, huh?
Yeah. He told me he played with Jimmy Gunn and they recorded one of his tunes to my levy home.
I've been hunting for that record ever since. Kildee, you mean? No, Herman Franklin. Oh, yeah.
He worked with Celestan, I don't know if they didn't record.
He wasn't recording like today, you know, doing that time.

Well with Herman, Herman had been away from old for many years. Yeah, he was definitely doing good. And when he came back and he went to Celestan and after Celestan he settled down, or not fool around anymore, and then he went into business and all like that until he died. He was on the road for years playing with different bands. Yeah.
